added_lemmas.statement:
For every fixed known \(x_0\in[0,1]^d\) and every parameter tuple satisfying \(S\le S_\star\), the estimator in \(\mathrm{def:total\mbox{-}estimator}\) obeys
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)}
\mathbb E_{P_O^{\otimes n}}|\widehat\tau_n(x_0)-\tau_P(x_0)|
\le C\{h_n^\gamma+\ell_n^S+(nh_n^d)^{-1/2}+\sqrt{K_n}/(nh_n^d)\}
\le C\rho_n
\]
for all \(n\ge2\), with \(C\) depending only on \((d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\).  At \(S=S_\star\), the last quantity is \(Cn^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\) and contains no logarithmic factor.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix the known point \(x_0\in[0,1]^d\), put \(D=[0,1]^d\), \(p=3/8\), \(h=h_n\), \(\bar h=h/2\), \(M=M_n\), and \(K=K_n\), and use the signs and coordinates from \(\mathrm{def:corrected\mbox{-}moments}\).  Because \(\sigma_k=1\) when \(x_{0k}\le 1/2\) and \(\sigma_k=-1\) otherwise,
\[
 \Phi_{x_0,h}(z)=x_0+\bar h\,\sigma\odot z\in D
 \quad (z\in D).                                                    \tag{1}
\]
Indeed, in the first case \(0\le \bar h z_k\le1/2\le1-x_{0k}\), and in the second \(0\le\bar h z_k\le1/2\le x_{0k}\).  Thus the local rectangle is never truncated, even when \(x_0\) lies on a face, edge, or corner.  Uniform design and the absolute Jacobian \(\bar h^d\) give, for every integrable \(u\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\bar h^{-d}\mathbf1\{Z_i\in D\}u(Z_i)\right]
 =\int_Du(z)\,dz.                                                     \tag{2}
\]
Reflection does not change the sup norm, and composition with \(\Phi_{x_0,h}\) multiplies an order-\(r\) derivative by at most \(\bar h^r\).  Hence all H\"older estimates below are uniform in \(x_0\).

Let \(\Pi_M\) be Lebesgue orthogonal projection onto the piecewise-polynomial space generated by \(b_{M_n}\), applied coordinatewise to vectors.  Taylor's formula on each cell of side \(M^{-1}\), the H\"older assumptions, and the degree choice \(p_{\mathrm{deg}}\) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \|(I-\Pi_M)\{v_j(e\circ\Phi_{x_0,h}-p)\}\|_2&\le C \ell^\alpha,\\
 \|(I-\Pi_M)\{v_j(e\circ\Phi_{x_0,h})\}\|_2&\le C \ell^\alpha,\\
 \|(I-\Pi_M)\{\mu_0\circ\Phi_{x_0,h}-1/2\}\|_2&\le C \ell^\beta. \tag{3}
\end{aligned}
\]
Here \(e=e_P\) and \(\mu_0=\mu_{0,P}\).  The compositions with \(\Phi_{x_0,h}\) have H\"older moduli bounded by \(C\bar h^\alpha\) and \(C\bar h^\beta\), and multiplication by a fixed-degree component of \(v\) preserves these bounds up to a fixed constant.  The cellwise errors are consequently \(C(\bar h/M)^\alpha\) and \(C(\bar h/M)^\beta\).  Constants of two are absorbed in (3), where \(\ell=h/M\).

Set \(e_h=e\circ\Phi_{x_0,h}\), \(\tau_h=\tau_P\circ\Phi_{x_0,h}\), and
\[
 Q=\int_D vv^{\mathsf T}e_h(1-e_h),\qquad
 R=\int_Dv e_h(1-e_h)\tau_h .                                       \tag{4}
\]
The propensity assumptions give \(1/4\le e_h\le1/2\).  Orthonormality of \(v\) therefore gives
\[
 u^{\mathsf T}Qu\ge\frac3{16}\int_D(u^{\mathsf T}v)^2
 =\lambda_0\|u\|_2^2,\qquad \lambda_0=3/16.                         \tag{5}
\]
Let \(\theta=Q^{-1}R\).  Equation (5), boundedness of the fixed vector \(v\), \(0\le e_h(1-e_h)\le1/4\), and \(|\tau_h|\le3/4\) imply \(\|\theta\|_2\le C\).  Taylor's formula of order \(\lceil\gamma\rceil-1\), followed by the normal equations in (4), yields
\[
 \sup_{z\in D}|v(z)^{\mathsf T}\theta-\tau_h(z)|\le C h^\gamma,
 \qquad |v(0)^{\mathsf T}\theta-\tau_P(x_0)|\le Ch^\gamma.          \tag{6}
\]
This step uses \(\Phi_{x_0,h}(0)=x_0\), and is therefore valid without assigning a conditional mean on a null event.

We next calculate the correction bias.  Conditional Bernoulli algebra gives
\[
 \mathbb E[A(A-p)\mid X]=e(1-p),                                    \tag{7}
\]
\[
 \mathbb E[(Y-1/2)(A-p)\mid X]
 =(e-p)(\mu_0-1/2)+e(1-p)\tau_P,                                   \tag{8}
\]
and \(\mathbb E[A-p\mid X]=e-p\), \(\mathbb E[A\mid X]=e\), and
\(\mathbb E[Y-1/2\mid X]=\mu_0-1/2+e\tau_P\).  Applying (2) to the linear term and independence to each ordered pair in the quadratic term shows, with bars denoting expectations, that
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \bar Q&=\int_Dvv^{\mathsf T}e_h(1-p)
 -\int_D\Pi_M\{v(e_h-p)\}e_hv^{\mathsf T},\\
 \bar R&=\int_Dv\{(e_h-p)(\mu_{0,h}-1/2)+e_h(1-p)\tau_h\}\\
 &\hspace{23mm}-\int_D\Pi_M\{v(e_h-p)\}\{\mu_{0,h}-1/2+e_h\tau_h\}. \tag{9}
\end{aligned}
\]
Projection orthogonality, (3), and Cauchy--Schwarz imply
\[
 \|\bar Q-Q\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le C\ell^{2\alpha}.                    \tag{10}
\]
Writing \(\Delta=\tau_h-v^{\mathsf T}\theta\), subtracting \(\bar Q\theta\) from \(\bar R\), and using \(Q\theta=R\) gives the exact residual identity
\[
 \bar R-\bar Q\theta
 =\int_D(I-\Pi_M)\{v(e_h-p)\}
          (I-\Pi_M)\{\mu_{0,h}-1/2+e_h\Delta\}.                    \tag{11}
\]
Equations (3), (6), projection contraction, and \(S=\alpha+\beta\) now yield
\[
 \|\bar R-\bar Q\theta\|_2\le C\{\ell^S+\ell^\alpha h^\gamma\}
 \le C(\ell^S+h^\gamma).                                           \tag{12}
\]

For completeness, the stochastic scale follows directly from the Hoeffding decomposition of the displayed ordered-pair statistics.  The linear projections are supported on a set of probability \(\bar h^d\), the weights are \(\bar h^{-d}\), and \(q\) is fixed.  Their coordinate variances are therefore at most \(C\bar h^{-d}\).  For the degenerate projections, the identity \(\int_D b_{M_n}b_{M_n}^{\mathsf T}=I_K\) gives the sum of coordinatewise second moments \(C K\bar h^{-2d}\).  Jensen's inequality and the finite-dimensional comparison between Euclidean and operator norms consequently give
\[
 \mathbb E\|\widetilde Q_n-\bar Q\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 +\mathbb E\|\widetilde R_n-\bar R\|_2
 \le C\left\{(nh^d)^{-1/2}+\frac{\sqrt K}{nh^d}\right\}.          \tag{13}
\]
All cell variables are bounded because \(A,Y\) are binary and the fixed-degree bases have finite sup norm; thus no unlisted moment or tail assumption is used in (13).

For sufficiently large \(n\), (10) is at most \(\lambda_0/4\).  On the event \(\|\widetilde Q_n-\bar Q\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\lambda_0/4\), (5) implies \(s_{\min}(\widetilde Q_n)\ge\lambda_0/2\), so the nonsingular branch is taken and \(\|\widetilde Q_n^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2/\lambda_0\).  On its complement, Markov's inequality and (13), together with clipping and \(|\tau_P(x_0)|\le3/4\), bound the risk by the right side of (13).  On the good event, (6), (12), (13), and
\[
 \widetilde Q_n^{-1}\widetilde R_n-\theta
 =\widetilde Q_n^{-1}(\widetilde R_n-\widetilde Q_n\theta)           \tag{14}
\]
give the same bound.  The finitely many smaller \(n\) are absorbed by increasing a constant depending only on the fixed parameters.  Since clipping onto \([-3/4,3/4]\) cannot increase distance from \(\tau_P(x_0)\), we obtain, uniformly in \(P\) and \(x_0\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P|\widehat\tau_n(x_0)-\tau_P(x_0)|
 \le C\left\{h^\gamma+\ell^S+(nh^d)^{-1/2}+\frac{\sqrt K}{nh^d}\right\}. \tag{15}
\]

It remains to evaluate the deterministic tuning in the closed regime.  Because \(S\le S_\star=d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)<\gamma\), \(M\le2n^{\eta(1/S-1/\gamma)}\), while its defining ceiling also gives the reverse inequality without the factor two.  Hence
\[
 h^\gamma=n^{-\eta},\qquad
 \ell^S\le n^{-\eta},                                               \tag{16}
\]
and \(S\le S_\star\) is algebraically equivalent to
\[
 \frac12-\frac{\eta d}{2\gamma}\ge\eta,
 \quad\text{so}\quad (nh^d)^{-1/2}\le n^{-\eta}.                  \tag{17}
\]
Finally, using \(K\le C M^d\) and the definition of \(\eta\),
\[
 \frac{\sqrt K}{nh^d}
 \le Cn^{-1+\eta d/(2\gamma)+\eta d/(2S)}
 =Cn^{-\eta}.                                                       \tag{18}
\]
Equations (15)--(18) prove the claim.  At \(S=S_\star\), \(\eta=\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), and every equality above is between pure powers; in particular, no logarithmic factor is introduced.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every fixed known \(x_0\in[0,1]^d\), every \(n\ge2\), and every parameter tuple satisfying \(S\le S_\star\), there are two finite priors \(\Pi_+,\Pi_-\) on \(\mathcal P(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\) with constant target values separated by at least \(c\rho_n\), whose genuine fixed-\(n\) observed-data mixtures satisfy
\[
H^2\!\left(\int P_O^{\otimes n}\,d\Pi_+,\int P_O^{\otimes n}\,d\Pi_-\right)\le\frac14.
\]
The conditional sign mixtures agree on singleton components, every component of size \(r\ge2\) obeys
\[
H^2(Q_{r,+},Q_{r,-})\le Ca^2b^2r^4(9/2)^r,
\]
and the full squared Hellinger distance is at most \(Cn^2h^d\ell^da^2b^2\).  The priors retain exact uniform covariate support and require neither Poissonization nor an occupancy event.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
We construct the priors directly for the fixed point \(x_0\) and the fixed sample size \(n\).  Let \(D=[0,1]^d\), \(p=3/8\), and choose a nonnegative \(C^\infty\) function \(k:\mathbb R^d\to[0,1]\), supported on \([-1,1]^d\), with \(k(0)=1\).  For example, normalize the product of \(e^{-1/(1-t^2)}\mathbf1\{|t|<1\}\) in the coordinates.  Put
\[
 k_{x_0,h}(x)=k\!\left(\frac{\sigma\odot(x-x_0)}h\right),
 \qquad K_{x_0,h}(x)=k_{x_0,h}(x)^2,                                \tag{19}
\]
where \(\sigma_k=1\) if \(x_{0k}\le1/2\) and \(\sigma_k=-1\) otherwise.  Symmetry of the support makes the sign immaterial to its size, but the orientation identifies an inward face at a boundary point.  The restriction of (19) to \(D\) is smooth, equals one at \(x_0\), and has active volume at most \((2h)^d\); truncation by the boundary only decreases that volume.  Thus boundary points require no extension of the design support.

At scale \(\ell\), put
\[
 J_\ell=\{j\in\mathbb Z^d:\operatorname{dist}_\infty(\ell j,D)\le\ell\},\qquad
 \phi_j(x)=\prod_{k=1}^d e^{-1/(1-(x_k/\ell-j_k)^2)}
                    \mathbf1\{|x_k/\ell-j_k|<1\},
\]
\[
 A_\ell(x)=\sum_{j\in J_\ell}\phi_j(x)^2,\qquad
 \psi_j(x)=\phi_j(x)A_\ell(x)^{-1/2}.
\]
The set \(J_\ell\) is finite.  Nearest-integer rounding gives an active translate within distance \(1/2\) in every coordinate, so \(A_\ell\) is bounded below by a positive constant on a neighborhood of \(D\).  The quotient rule and scaling therefore give
\[
 \sum_j\psi_j(x)^2=1,\quad
 \operatorname{supp}(\psi_j)\subseteq\{x:\|x-\ell j\|_\infty\le\ell\},\quad
 \|D^\nu\psi_j\|_\infty\le C_\nu\ell^{-|\nu|},                  \tag{20}
\]
and at most \(3^d\) functions are active at one point.

For independent Rademacher signs \(\vartheta_j\), define
\[
 F_\vartheta(x)=k_{x_0,h}(x)\sum_j\vartheta_j\psi_j(x),\qquad K(x)=K_{x_0,h}(x). \tag{21}
\]
Then, with \(B=3^{d/2}\),
\[
 \mathbb E_\vartheta F_\vartheta=0,\qquad
 \mathbb E_\vartheta F_\vartheta^2=K,\qquad
 |F_\vartheta|\le B.                                                \tag{22}
\]
The product rule, (20), and \(\ell\le h\) show for every fixed \(s>0\) that
\[
 \|F_\vartheta\|_{\mathcal H_d^s(1)}\le C_s\ell^{-s},\qquad
 \|K\|_{\mathcal H_d^s(1)}\le C_sh^{-s}.                           \tag{23}
\]
For the fractional seminorm in (23), an order-\(m=\lceil s\rceil-1\) derivative is bounded both by \(Cr^{-m}\) and, by the mean-value theorem, by \(Cr^{-m-1}\|x-y\|_\infty\); splitting at \(\|x-y\|_\infty=r\) gives \(Cr^{-s}\|x-y\|_\infty^{s-m}\), including the integral case \(s-m=1\).

For \(\varepsilon\in\{-1,1\}\), define
\[
\begin{aligned}
 e_\vartheta&=p+aF_\vartheta,\\
 \mu_{0,\varepsilon,\vartheta}&=\frac12+\varepsilon bF_\vartheta
       +\frac{\varepsilon ab}{1-p}K,\\
 \tau_\varepsilon&=-\frac{\varepsilon ab}{p(1-p)}K,\\
 \mu_{1,\varepsilon,\vartheta}&=\frac12+\varepsilon bF_\vartheta
       -\frac{\varepsilon ab}{p}K.                                  \tag{24}
\end{aligned}
\]
Choose
\[
 \ell=c_\ell n^{-\eta/S},\qquad h=\ell^{S/\gamma},\qquad
 a=c_a\ell^\alpha,\qquad b=c_b\ell^\beta.                           \tag{25}
\]
Because \(S\le S_\star<\gamma\), \(0<\ell\le h\le1\).  Equations (23)--(25) give
\[
 a\ell^{-\alpha}=c_a,\quad b\ell^{-\beta}=c_b,\quad
 ab h^{-\gamma}=c_ac_b,\quad
 ab h^{-\beta}=c_ac_b\ell^{S(1-\beta/\gamma)}\le c_ac_b.             \tag{26}
\]
Starting from the constants \(4p=3/2\) and \(1/2\), choose the positive constants \(c_a,c_b\) sufficiently small, depending only on the fixed parameters.  The defining derivative and seminorm bounds in (23), (26), and \(L\ge4\) then prove
\[
 4e_\vartheta\in\mathcal H_d^\alpha(L),\quad 1\le4e_\vartheta\le2,\quad
 \mu_{0,\varepsilon,\vartheta}\in\mathcal H_d^\beta(L),\quad
 \tau_\varepsilon\in\mathcal H_d^\gamma(L),\quad
 \frac18\le\mu_{a,\varepsilon,\vartheta}\le\frac78.                \tag{27}
\]
For each \((\varepsilon,\vartheta)\), draw \(X\) exactly uniformly on \(D\), draw \(A\mid X=x\) as Bernoulli \(e_\vartheta(x)\), draw the two potential outcomes conditionally independently with the means in (24), independently of \(A\) given \(X\), and set \(Y=AY(1)+(1-A)Y(0)\).  Thus consistency and conditional exchangeability hold by construction, the response law is Bernoulli, and (27) proves membership in \(\mathcal P(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\).  Let \(\Pi_\varepsilon\) be uniform over the finite sign vectors.  Since \(K(x_0)=1\), its target is constant and
\[
 |\tau_+(x_0)-\tau_-(x_0)|=\frac{2ab}{p(1-p)}.                       \tag{28}
\]

We next prove the mixture bound for the actual fixed-\(n\) product experiment.  At a fixed \(x\), replace \((a,\varepsilon b)\) by real variables \((s,t)\) in (24).  In the four cells \((A,Y)=(1,1),(1,0),(0,1),(0,0)\), direct multiplication gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
q_{11}&=p/2+sF/2+ptF+st(F^2-K)-s^2tKF/p,\\
q_{10}&=p/2+sF/2-ptF-st(F^2-K)+s^2tKF/p,\\
q_{01}&=(1-p)/2-sF/2+(1-p)tF-st(F^2-K)-s^2tKF/(1-p),\\
q_{00}&=(1-p)/2-sF/2-(1-p)tF+st(F^2-K)+s^2tKF/(1-p).                 \tag{29}
\end{aligned}
\]
Using (22) in (29) shows that the sign average of each cell is the corresponding coordinate of
\(q_0=(p/2,p/2,(1-p)/2,(1-p)/2)\), independently of the sign of \(t\).  Thus every singleton component agrees exactly; there is no singleton leakage.

After decreasing \(c_a,c_b\), all ratios \(q_z/q_{0,z}\) lie in \([1/2,3/2]\), and their first \(s\), first \(t\), and mixed derivatives are bounded by a constant.  For fixed locations \(x_1,\ldots,x_r\), let
\[
 M_r(s,t;z_{1:r})=\mathbb E_\vartheta\prod_{i=1}^r
 \frac{q_{z_i}(s,t;x_i)}{q_{0,z_i}}.
\]
The product rule has \(r\) terms with both derivatives on one factor and \(r(r-1)\) with derivatives on distinct factors, whence
\[
 |\partial_s\partial_tM_r(s,t;z_{1:r})|\le Cr^2(3/2)^r.              \tag{30}
\]
At \(s=0\), the transformation \(\vartheta\mapsto-\vartheta\) shows \(M_r(0,b)=M_r(0,-b)\).  Twice applying the fundamental theorem of calculus to (30), and using \(M_r\ge2^{-r}\), gives
\[
 H^2(Q_{r,+},Q_{r,-})\le Ca^2b^2r^4(9/2)^r,\qquad r\ge2.             \tag{31}
\]

Condition on the realized \(X_{1:n}\).  Retain observations in the support of \(k_{x_0,h}\), and connect \(i,j\) when \(\|X_i-X_j\|_\infty\le2\ell\).  By (20), different connected components use disjoint sign coordinates, so the conditional mixture factors over components.  Product Hellinger affinities and \(1-\prod_j u_j\le\sum_j(1-u_j)\) imply that the conditional squared Hellinger distance is at most the sum of (31).  If \(N_r\) is the number of size-\(r\) components, a connected labeled set contains a spanning tree.  Deleting the least labeled leaf successively records a word of length \(r-2\) over the \(r\) labels; the reverse procedure, which adjoins the least label absent from the remaining word, reconstructs the unique tree.  This bijection gives exactly \(r^{r-2}\) labeled trees.  Sequential integration of a root and its children therefore gives
\[
 \mathbb E N_r\le {n\choose r}r^{r-2}(2h)^d(4\ell)^{d(r-1)}.         \tag{32}
\]
Because \(r!\ge(r/e)^r\), (31)--(32) yield
\[
 \mathbb E_XH^2\{\mathsf M_+(\cdot\mid X_{1:n}),\mathsf M_-(\cdot\mid X_{1:n})\}
 \le Cn^2h^d\ell^da^2b^2                                          \tag{33}
\]
provided \(C_0n\ell^d\le1/2\); this follows by summing the resulting geometric series beginning at \(r=2\).  Both mixtures have the same uniform \(X_{1:n}\)-marginal, so integrating the conditional Hellinger affinity shows that (33) is exactly the unconditional fixed-\(n\) squared Hellinger bound.  No conditioning event and no Poissonization has been used.

Finally,
\[
 1-\frac{d\eta}{S}\le0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad S\le\frac{d\gamma}{2\gamma+d}=S_\star. \tag{34}
\]
Hence \(n\ell^d\le c_\ell^d\); at equality it is exactly \(c_\ell^d\), so choosing \(c_\ell\) small proves the series condition rather than producing a logarithm.  Moreover,
\[
 n^2h^d\ell^da^2b^2
 =c_a^2c_b^2 n^2\ell^{2S+d+Sd/\gamma}=C(c_a,c_b,c_\ell),             \tag{35}
\]
because \(\eta(2+d/S+d/\gamma)=2\).  Decreasing \(c_\ell>0\) makes (33) at most \(1/4\), while (28) becomes
\[
 |\tau_+(x_0)-\tau_-(x_0)|
 =\frac{2c_ac_bc_\ell^S}{p(1-p)}n^{-\eta}=c\rho_n.                  \tag{36}
\]
All constants are positive and depend only on \((d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\), uniformly over \(x_0\).  This proves every asserted support, separation, component, and fixed-product property.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Fix any known \(x_0\in[0,1]^d\).  There exist constants \(0<c\le C<\infty\), depending only on \((d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\) and uniform in \(x_0\), such that, for every \(n\ge2\) and \(S\le S_\star\),
\[
c\rho_n\le R_n\le C\rho_n,\qquad
\rho_n=n^{-1/(1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2(\alpha+\beta)))}.
\]
The upper bound is attained by the total finite estimator \(\widehat\tau_n(x_0)\), and the lower bound uses genuine fixed-\(n\) product laws in the same exact-uniform, bounded-overlap Bernoulli class.  At \(S=S_\star\), the rate is exactly \(n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\) with no logarithmic multiplier; for \(S<S_\star\), it is strictly slower than that oracle power.  Consequently, the lower bound transfers by set inclusion to any model containing this exact class and using the same point target; no corresponding upper bound is asserted.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The active directive requires the fixed-point and closed-regime formulation.  The claim remains on the identical exact-uniform law class and is proved directly by the two new technical lemmas.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
\[
R_n(x_0)=\inf_{T\ \mathrm{Borel}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)}
\mathbb E_{P_O^{\otimes n}}\!\left|T(O_{1:n})-\tau_P(x_0)\right|.
\]
Because \(x_0\) is fixed and known throughout the note, write this quantity as \(R_n\).
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The risk must evaluate the directed fixed known point rather than only the corner.
The rate definition now explicitly records the closed at-or-below-elbow domain.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Put \(h=h_n\), \(\bar h=h/2\), and, for \(k=1,\ldots,d\), set \(\sigma_k=1\) if \(x_{0k}\le1/2\) and \(\sigma_k=-1\) otherwise.  Define the inward affine chart
\[
\Phi_{x_0,h}(z)=x_0+\bar h\,\sigma\odot z,\qquad z\in[0,1]^d,
\]
whose image lies in \([0,1]^d\), and define
\[
Z_i=\bar h^{-1}\sigma\odot(X_i-x_0),\quad I_i=\mathbf1\{Z_i\in[0,1]^d\},\quad
w_i=\bar h^{-d}I_i,\quad v_i=v(Z_i)I_i,\quad b_i=b_{M_n}(Z_i)I_i.
\]
Every zero-indicator product is evaluated before an outside-domain basis value.  With \(p=3/8\), define
\[
\widetilde Q_n=\frac1n\sum_iw_iv_iA_i(A_i-p)v_i^{\mathsf T}
-\frac1{n(n-1)}\sum_{i\ne j}w_iw_jv_i(A_i-p)(b_i^{\mathsf T}b_j)A_jv_j^{\mathsf T},
\]
\[
\widetilde R_n=\frac1n\sum_iw_iv_i(Y_i-1/2)(A_i-p)
-\frac1{n(n-1)}\sum_{i\ne j}w_iw_jv_i(A_i-p)(b_i^{\mathsf T}b_j)(Y_j-1/2).
\]
The factor \(\bar h=h_n/2\) makes the full chart available at every boundary or interior location; reflection has unit absolute Jacobian and the remaining constant factor is absorbed in rate constants.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The moment construction needs a reflected inward chart to use the same fixed local cube at every boundary or interior point.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
With \(\lambda_0=3/16\), define
\[
\widehat\tau_n(x_0)=
\begin{cases}
0,&s_{\min}(\widetilde Q_n)<\lambda_0/2,\\
\operatorname{clip}_{[-3/4,3/4]}\!\left(v(0)^{\mathsf T}\widetilde Q_n^{-1}\widetilde R_n\right),
&s_{\min}(\widetilde Q_n)\ge\lambda_0/2.
\end{cases}
\]
The inward chart, branch rule, half-open cells, fixed basis order, ceiling in \(M_n\), and clipping make this a finite total Borel algorithm on every data set.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The total estimator now reports the contrast at the fixed known point through the translated moments.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: For the fixed known \(x_0\), construct \(\mathfrak H_{n,x_0}^{\mathrm{comp}}\) by multiplying a smooth squared partition of unity at fine scale \(\ell\) by a translated compact \(C^\infty\) localization bump that equals one at \(x_0\), using shared Rademacher coefficients and joint \((A,Y)\)-cell perturbations that cancel after one sign average.  Conditional on \(X_{1:n}\), connect observations whose active frames share a coefficient, factor the mixture over connected components, control each non-singleton component through a mixed amplitude derivative, and sum connected subsets by labeled spanning trees.  The localization is restricted to \([0,1]^d\); at a boundary point this only reduces its active volume and never changes the exact uniform design.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The lower construction handle must name the translated compact localization and its boundary behavior.

proposed.name: corrected local moments
proposed.construction:
Put \(h=h_n\), \(\bar h=h/2\), and, for \(k=1,\ldots,d\), set \(\sigma_k=1\) if \(x_{0k}\le1/2\) and \(\sigma_k=-1\) otherwise.  Define the inward affine chart
\[
\Phi_{x_0,h}(z)=x_0+\bar h\,\sigma\odot z,\qquad z\in[0,1]^d,
\]
whose image lies in \([0,1]^d\), and define
\[
Z_i=\bar h^{-1}\sigma\odot(X_i-x_0),\quad I_i=\mathbf1\{Z_i\in[0,1]^d\},\quad
w_i=\bar h^{-d}I_i,\quad v_i=v(Z_i)I_i,\quad b_i=b_{M_n}(Z_i)I_i.
\]
Every zero-indicator product is evaluated before an outside-domain basis value.  With \(p=3/8\), define
\[
\widetilde Q_n=\frac1n\sum_iw_iv_iA_i(A_i-p)v_i^{\mathsf T}
-\frac1{n(n-1)}\sum_{i\ne j}w_iw_jv_i(A_i-p)(b_i^{\mathsf T}b_j)A_jv_j^{\mathsf T},
\]
\[
\widetilde R_n=\frac1n\sum_iw_iv_i(Y_i-1/2)(A_i-p)
-\frac1{n(n-1)}\sum_{i\ne j}w_iw_jv_i(A_i-p)(b_i^{\mathsf T}b_j)(Y_j-1/2).
\]
The factor \(\bar h=h_n/2\) makes the full chart available at every boundary or interior location; reflection has unit absolute Jacobian and the remaining constant factor is absorbed in rate constants.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The complete construction now includes the inward chart and target-point symbol.

proposed.name: That
proposed.construction:
With \(\lambda_0=3/16\), define
\[
\widehat\tau_n(x_0)=
\begin{cases}
0,&s_{\min}(\widetilde Q_n)<\lambda_0/2,\\
\operatorname{clip}_{[-3/4,3/4]}\!\left(v(0)^{\mathsf T}\widetilde Q_n^{-1}\widetilde R_n\right),
&s_{\min}(\widetilde Q_n)\ge\lambda_0/2.
\end{cases}
\]
The inward chart, branch rule, half-open cells, fixed basis order, ceiling in \(M_n\), and clipping make this a finite total Borel algorithm on every data set.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The estimator construction now consumes the translated moments and returns the fixed-point estimate.

proposed.name: ComponentHandle
proposed.construction: For the fixed known \(x_0\), construct \(\mathfrak H_{n,x_0}^{\mathrm{comp}}\) by multiplying a smooth squared partition of unity at fine scale \(\ell\) by a translated compact \(C^\infty\) localization bump that equals one at \(x_0\), using shared Rademacher coefficients and joint \((A,Y)\)-cell perturbations that cancel after one sign average.  Conditional on \(X_{1:n}\), connect observations whose active frames share a coefficient, factor the mixture over connected components, control each non-singleton component through a mixed amplitude derivative, and sum connected subsets by labeled spanning trees.  The localization is restricted to \([0,1]^d\); at a boundary point this only reduces its active volume and never changes the exact uniform design.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The construction handle must be coherent with the translated converse.

proposed.statement:
Fix any known \(x_0\in[0,1]^d\).  There exist constants \(0<c\le C<\infty\), depending only on \((d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\) and uniform in \(x_0\), such that, for every \(n\ge2\) and \(S\le S_\star\),
\[
c\rho_n\le R_n\le C\rho_n,\qquad
\rho_n=n^{-1/(1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2(\alpha+\beta)))}.
\]
The upper bound is attained by the total finite estimator \(\widehat\tau_n(x_0)\), and the lower bound uses genuine fixed-\(n\) product laws in the same exact-uniform, bounded-overlap Bernoulli class.  At \(S=S_\star\), the rate is exactly \(n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\) with no logarithmic multiplier; for \(S<S_\star\), it is strictly slower than that oracle power.  Consequently, the lower bound transfers by set inclusion to any model containing this exact class and using the same point target; no corresponding upper bound is asserted.
proposed.justification: The theorem determines the exact-uniform minimax order at every fixed known point throughout the closed at-or-below-elbow regime.
proposed.gap: The published general-design lower construction does not prove the converse after fixing the design to exact uniformity; the component prior supplies that missing same-class certificate.
proposed.consumer: Users obtain an exact pointwise CATE precision benchmark, including the no-log oracle equality at the elbow.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The headline statement now depends directly on the two proved fixed-point closed-regime lemmas.

prose_updates.tldr:
For every fixed known \(x_0\in[0,1]^d\), the exact-uniform bounded-overlap Bernoulli model has sharp pointwise CATE risk
\[
R_n\asymp n^{-1/(1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2(\alpha+\beta)))}
\]
throughout \(S=\alpha+\beta\le d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\).  A reflected inward local projection estimator attains the rate on every data set, and a translated correlated-sign component prior proves the genuine fixed-\(n\) same-class converse.  At the elbow the rate is exactly \(n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\), with no logarithmic multiplier; strictly below it, nuisance learning causes an unavoidable slower power.

project_justification.gap: The published pointwise CATE theory gives this candidate power on a broader model, but its displayed lower laws delete design mass around nuisance-bump transitions.  A lower bound on that broader class does not imply the same bound after fixing \(P_X\) to the exact uniform law, and it does not by itself certify arbitrary boundary or interior point targets on the singleton class.
project_justification.niche: The note isolates the exact known-uniform, bounded-overlap Bernoulli/interiority subclass and asks only for its pointwise estimation and inference benchmark.  The class is a strict subclass of the published general-design model, so a same-class converse is the missing ingredient; identification is already supplied by consistency, exchangeability, overlap, full support, and continuity.
project_justification.fill: A reflected inward chart gives one total finite projection \(U\)-statistic estimator uniformly over fixed \(x_0\).  For the converse, a translated compact smooth window and squared frame partition make singleton sign mixtures agree exactly; sparse component factorization, a mixed-amplitude Hellinger bound, and spanning-tree enumeration control the full fixed-\(n\) mixture.  At equality, \(n\ell^d\) is a tunably small constant, which closes the elbow without a logarithm.

prose_updates.related_work: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE is the closest comparator: its theorems provide the nuisance-elbow pointwise CATE architecture on a broader design-density model, whereas the present result closes the fixed-\(n\) converse on the strict exact-uniform bounded-overlap Bernoulli/interiority subclass.  The lower converse therefore transfers upward by subclass inclusion to any broader model that contains this subclass and uses the same point target; the exact-uniform upper proof does not transfer in that direction and is not claimed there.  RobinsTchetgenLiVanderVaart2009SemiparametricMinimax supplies the product-mixture perspective, but the shared smooth frames here require random overlap-component factorization rather than a deterministic coordinate-local partition.  ShenGaoWittenHan2020Variance is a random-design nonlinear-functional analogue for repeated local occupancy.  Kennedy2023DRCATE and NieWager2021RLearner provide oracle-facing upper comparisons, while RobinsLiTchetgenVanderVaart2008HOIF motivates the finite projection correction.  WagerAthey2018CausalForests is an application-facing consumer: this is a precision benchmark for \(\texttt{causal\_forest}\) and R-learner workflows, not a claim that existing forests attain the bound.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The sparse-component summation uses \(n\ell^d\le C\) and therefore certifies only the at-or-below-elbow regime; above the elbow the present prior is not a converse certificate.  The finite estimator also uses the known smoothness tuple in its deterministic bandwidth and projection dimension.  Constants are not optimized, and the theorem concerns mean absolute pointwise risk rather than a confidence procedure.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved contribution is the same-class full-support fixed-\(n\) lower bound, paired with a total finite estimator, for every fixed known \(x_0\in[0,1]^d\) and \(S\le S_\star\).  It includes boundary points through a reflected inward chart and proves the exact no-log oracle power at \(S=S_\star\).  The exact-uniform class is a strict subclass of the published general-design class: only the lower bound transfers upward by subclass inclusion at matching point targets.  The note does not claim its upper bound for unknown or nonuniform design, and it does not treat \(\kappa>0\) local overlap decay, adaptive tuning, confidence intervals, integrated loss, or performance guarantees for existing causal forests.
